# CLAUDE.md Atharva Shah's Obsidian Vault

## How to talk to me

1. Write every response in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.
2. Talk to me like I have ADHD, because I do.

## What This Is

This is my Obsidian knowledge vault. It's a local-first, plain-text system for ideation, writing, publishing, and content distribution. Everything is Markdown. Everything is portable. No vendor lock-in.

## Why This Vault Exists

This is the whole purpose of the vault, so read it before you touch anything in here.

The vault is a brain transplant. Every file exists to move something out of my head and into a system that produces the same result when I am not present.

The test comes from [Business Is Hard Until You Do This](LIBRARY/Notes/Business%20Is%20Hard%20Until%20You%20Do%20This%20-%20Michia%20Rohrssen.md). If I disappeared for two weeks, could someone who has never met me open this repo and keep the whole operation running? Every commit either moves that answer toward yes or wastes my time.

That reframes what each folder is for. `DIGITAL TWIN/` exists so my voice and judgment survive outside my skull. `SCRIPTS/` and `.claude/skills/` exist so work that never needed a brain stops reaching mine.

The scorers and gates exist so recurring decisions get made once and enforced forever. `SUBSTACK/` is a production line with an owner and a done condition at every stage. The sitemap and `graphify-out/` exist so none of it needs me as the search engine.

Three consequences that override convenience:

- An SOP that a stranger cannot follow end to end without asking me a question is not finished. The stranger here is a fresh model with no session history, which is a harder test than a new hire.
- Undocumented knowledge that lives only in my head or in a chat session is a defect, so write it down where the vault can find it.
- A rule belongs in code or in a README, never in a one-off instruction I have to repeat.

## Vault Structure

```
INBOX/               ← Active & unprocessed captures. Anything loose at the root is untriaged.
  Ideas/             ← Raw idea captures waiting to become an article, product, or project.
  Reports/           ← Recurring routine output: Flywheel Review, Pipeline Health, Draft Queue, handoffs.
  Admin/             ← Money, legal, applications, coursework, personal obligations.
  Webinar/           ← DevRelUni May 2026 webinar script, slides, PDF.
  _images/           ← Loose screenshots no note references yet.
LIBRARY/             ← Stable & reference-grade: Glossary, Guides, Lists, Notes, Resources.
ARCHIVE/             ← Retired notes. Never delete, always archive.
DIGITAL TWIN/        ← My identity files: About, Voice, Audience, Goals, Principles, Experience, Socials.
  core/              ← Always loaded for any writing job. runtime-contract.md is the load order
                       and the check order. pattern-rules.md is the failure shapes the scorer
                       cannot see, plus what never to flag and what to protect. write-simply.md
                       is the plain style, and the test that a sentence reading badly means the
                       idea under it is wrong. net-new-value.md is the guiding principle: only a
                       non-obvious, tactical insight ships.
META/                ← Engine room: Attachments, Excalidraw, Templates. Never reorganize it.

  1_DRAFTS/          ← Work-in-progress articles (flat .md files, no nesting)

```

Both index systems (per-folder `index.html` and OKF `index.md`) were retired on 2026-08-27 and their pre-commit hook blocks were removed. Never regenerate either; `SCRIPTS/index/README.md` records why. The two hand-made `index.html` pages under `LIBRARY/Resources/GTM Engineering Automations/` are the only ones that remain, on purpose.

## Content Pipeline

### Substack Publishing Flow

`0_IDEAS` → `1_DRAFTS` → `2_PUBLISHED` → Social Flywheel. The full pipeline (frontmatter schema, SEO checklist, internal-linking model, sitemap SOP, scripts) lives in `SUBSTACK/README.md`, which is the single source of truth. Do not duplicate that detail here.

### Triage every new idea before writing it

The first question about any new article idea is whether it should exist at all, because a new idea that feels fresh is often the third pass at something already live.

**Whenever Atharva drops a blog idea, an article request, a topic, a headline, or asks whether to write about something, run this before drafting a single word:**

```bash
python SCRIPTS/substack/overlap.py check "<the idea in plain words>"
```

`ABSORB` or `MERGE` means do not start drafting. Say so, name the article that should absorb it, name what that article is missing, and propose the merge. Push back once, then respect his answer. On `WRITE` say nothing about overlap and just get on with it.

A `THIN` flag on a match means that article is long and low-density, which is the strongest merge case: the new idea is the substance that article was always missing. `overlap.py thin` ranks those, and `pairs` finds published articles that already duplicate each other.

Full procedure, the pushback script, the calibration probes and the merge workflow live in `.claude/skills/substack-idea-triage/SKILL.md`. Read it before proposing a merge.

### Social Flywheel (Content Distribution)

When a blog is published, the Templater creates empty placeholder files:

| Channel           | Folder                        | Prefix     | State          |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------- | -------------- |
| X / Twitter       | SOCIALS/Tweets/               | tweet\_    | `posted` flag  |
| LinkedIn post     | SOCIALS/LinkedIn/             | li\_       | folder         |
| LinkedIn carousel | SOCIALS/LinkedIn/<post-slug>/ | carousel\_ | folder (HTML)  |
| Substack Notes    | SOCIALS/Substack Notes/       | subnotes\_ | `posted` flag  |

# neatHack Build Log: FirstRun

## Project

- **Name:** FirstRun
- **Purpose:** FirstRun runs your quickstart in a clean container, finds the first step that breaks, and proves the fix with a second clean run.
- **Problem:** Quickstarts break when a package is renamed, a flag is removed or a version moves. Nobody on the team gets an alert. The first person who finds the break is a new user, and most new users leave.

## Team

- Atharva Shah ([@HighnessAtharva](https://github.com/HighnessAtharva)), solo.

## Stack

| Part | Tool |
|---|---|
| Language | Python 3.11 |
| Agent | Claude Agent SDK, model `claude-sonnet-5-5` at medium effort, auth through `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` |
| Tracing | neatlogs Python SDK 1.4.26, neatlogs CLI 0.2.0 |
| Sandbox | Docker Engine 29.8.2 in WSL Ubuntu 22.04, one fresh container per run |
| Docs reader | Firecrawl CLI 1.25.3 |
| Failure classifier | Jev (TypeSafe System One) |
| Session capture | Entire CLI 0.11.4: Checkpoints, Graph, Brain, Trails |
| Business plan | cfo.ai |

## Planning Happened Before the Event

Planning and tool tests happened before the event in a private repo. No FirstRun code was written before kickoff (Sat 2026-10-10, 12:30 PM IST).

## Build Log

### 2026-10-10 (Saturday)

- **12:30 to 13:10 IST.** Created the public repo, ran `entire enable --agent claude-code --search-skill --agent-help-skill` before commit 1, and pushed the Entire config, 6 Trail runners, and the Graph and Brain agent instructions.
- **13:20 IST.** Preflight passed: 4 keys present (lengths only checked), Docker 29.8.2 in WSL, `gh`, Firecrawl 1.25.3, Entire 0.11.4, the venv on Python 3.11. `entire doctor` reports no problems.
- **13:30 IST.** Scaffold: `pyproject.toml`, `src/firstrun/config.py` (the only file that names a model), `src/firstrun/tracing.py`.
  - `python -m neatlogs doctor --probe` passed 8 of 8 checks, including `TRACE_VISIBLE` and `TRACE_FINALIZED`.
  - The first FirstRun trace, `firstrun.hello`, is trace `fdcab847f3129a251c6ae45f00c76a1c`. It is finalized with 2 spans and tag `hello`, and the neatlogs CLI read it back.

Entire state at the scaffold commit, run by the build agent:

```text
$ entire status
● Enabled · branch main
  Agents · Claude Code
  Checkpoints sync to: origin
1 session

$ entire checkpoint list
  branch       main
  checkpoints  0
No checkpoints found on this branch.
```

The checkpoint count is 0 because the scaffold commit is the first commit made inside an agent session. Later entries record the count after it.

- **12:55 IST. Entire checkpoints hung on Git 2.33.** The post-commit hook waited 206 s on `git update-ref --stdin` and the checkpoint for the scaffold commit was never written. Upgrading Git for Windows to 2.55.0 fixed it: the next hook took 3 s and the checkpoint landed.
- **13:00 to 13:35 IST. Six worker agents built FirstRun in parallel** on main, one track each: fixtures, planner, executor, recovery, verify and output, report page. Each track is one commit with its own checkpoint.
- **13:35 IST. Layer 1 done.** `firstrun run https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/python` passed 4 of 4 steps in 70 s and wrote `report.md`. The first live run showed one run split into 3 neatlogs traces, so the CLI now opens one `firstrun.run` trace around reading, planning, every step and verification.

### v1 Runs, Layer 1 Only (Recovery Off), Tag `v1`

| Target | Result | Time | Cost (list price, not billed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| neatlogs Python SDK | passed 3/3 | 84 s | $0.036 |
| Entire CLI install | failed at step 1: `curl: command not found` on python:3.11-slim | n/a | $0.023 |
| Chroma getting started | passed 3/3 | 250 s | $0.029 |
| OpenAI v0 README (FIXTURE, Wayback 2023-08-02) | failed at step 6: `openai: command not found`, the documented CLI is gone from today's SDK | n/a | $0.031 |

neatlogs v1 traces, one `firstrun.run` trace per run, cost as neatlogs measured it:

| Target | Trace ID | Spans | Tool spans | LLM calls | neatlogs cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| neatlogs | `fccdbad9a9c6177b90112911fe485bd6` | 9 | 4 | 1 | $0.0397 |
| Entire | `10c44df9626c19f5ac801f1c6d84610e` | 7 | 2 | 1 | $0.0170 |
| Chroma | `66ec093b00333fa221fade5d2fc5f55f` | 9 | 4 | 1 | $0.0217 |
| OpenAI v0 FIXTURE | `b98b419e286acf436083febdb5217cf9` | 12 | 7 | 1 | $0.0266 |

Six mistakes the agent itself made in v1. These are the "before" story:

1. **The plan changes between runs.** The same neatlogs page gave 4 steps at 13:35 and 3 steps at 13:40.
2. **The planner invents steps.** It added `command -v entire`, `command -v git-remote-entire` and `test -f first_trace.py`, which are not in the docs.
3. **The planner writes placeholder steps.** Chroma step 2 is `true`, a no-op standing in for "create the file".
4. **A fake secret passes as a step.** The OpenAI step `export OPENAI_API_KEY='sk-...'` exits 0, so it counts as a pass while proving nothing.
5. **The planner skips the step that matters.** It dropped the OpenAI `openai.ChatCompletion.create` example and the neatlogs "run your app" step because they need a key. Those are the steps most likely to break.
6. **Most expected results check only the exit code.** 9 of 16 steps have no output check, so a command that prints an error and exits 0 would pass.

### Saturday Afternoon: neatlogs Found the Agent's Own Bug, and v2 Fixed It

- **14:10 IST.** Atharva created two neatlogs detections: "docs step broke" (TOOL spans) and "planner invented a step" (the planner span). The second flagged the planner spans of 3 v1 runs.
- **14:40 IST.** neatlogs Investigate (Deep, workflow `firstrun`) traced the invented steps to the planner prompt and proposed a stricter one ([evidence/neatlogs-investigation.md](evidence/neatlogs-investigation.md)).
- **14:45 IST.** A headless Claude Code session read the detection and its trend over the neatlogs MCP server and applied the fix with code guards and a plan cache: commit 3ca6f11, checkpoint `01M4JGJ6NTE7YNB9Z0YW5FYVHN`, [Entire commit view](https://entire.io/gh/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/commit/3ca6f118ecb0a8915315eea27b5588dd8a7c6299).
- **15:15 IST. v2 versus v1** on the same 4 targets: quickstarts finished 2 to 3 of 4, failed steps recovered 0 to 3, cost per run $0.0262 to $0.0200 (neatlogs). The v2 and real-world runs exposed 5 agent bugs, all fixed: a pipe that hid a missing `curl`, a multi-line step that hid a failing `pip`, pip noise that hid the real error, container fixes counted as docs bugs, and a file check after `cd`.

### Saturday Evening: Real Docs, Upstream PRs, and Entire Reviewing Every Layer

- **Real quickstarts:** dbt + DuckDB, AccuKnox knoxctl, Dagster, MkDocs and the Entire install all reached `verified` in a fresh container.
- **Upstream PRs, each from a verified run and a duplicate search:** [dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com#10149](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10149) (`jafgen --years` removed), [#10150](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10150) (Python 3.12 floor), [entireio/cli#2724](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2724) (Linux PATH after `install.sh`), [accuknox/help#671](https://github.com/accuknox/help/pull/671) (knoxctl page named 0.9.0 while the installer fetched 0.9.58).
- **No PR where the docs were right:** Dagster's page already covers both gaps FirstRun hit, so FirstRun opened nothing there. MkDocs needed only `curl` in the container.
- **Trails:** branch-backed Trails 3 to 8 cover every commit since kickoff. Entire runners raised 3 real bugs, all fixed and resolved with the commit SHA: a secret retry loop, a Windows-only Docker default, and a `cd` guard that was written but never called.
- **CI:** GitHub Actions runs the offline suite on every push. It caught 3 tests that passed only with a local Claude token.

### Saturday Night: Two New Answers From the Same Engine

- **Docs Bisect** (`firstrun bisect`): on the dbt guide, `jafgen --years 6` passes on jafgen 0.3.1 (2023-01-17) and fails on 0.4.6 (2024-04-07), and PyPI has no release between them. The guide merged on 2025-03-14, 11 months later. 5 probes, $0 in model calls. The evidence is a [comment on #10149](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10149#issuecomment-6096827074).
- **Prerequisite Proof** (`firstrun prereqs`): proven blocks for AccuKnox (curl, ca-certificates, gnupg, sudo, 5/5 steps), MkDocs (curl, 9/9 steps) and Entire (curl, git, `~/.local/bin` on PATH, 4/4 steps).
- **Website:** [1run.netlify.app](https://1run.netlify.app) takes a docs URL and writes a prompt for the visitor's own coding agent. A tested URL shows its cached run first. Every run prints a share link that replays read, plan, run, fix, prove, plus the bisect timeline and the assumptions card.
- **Jury self-test:** the Entire judge plugin ranked the repo with no excluded work, 3.93 of 5 ([evidence/jury-selftest.txt](evidence/jury-selftest.txt)).

### 2026-10-10, 17:45 to 18:05 IST: The Business Plan Sets the Agent's Budget

- **Done: `firstrun econ`.** The command reads 64 `firstrun.run` traces from neatlogs and writes [business/drivers.csv](business/drivers.csv) and [business/unit_economics.json](business/unit_economics.json). Mean cost per run is $0.0167, p95 is $0.0508 and max is $0.1014. Each quantile row names its trace ID.
- **Finding:** the fixed $0.50 cap in `models.py` was 30 times the mean run. If every run hit it, Scale margin would be -403.6%. At a 70% margin floor, the Scale cap is $0.028, and 25.0% of measured runs cost more than that. [business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md](business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md) gives two fixes from the same formula: Scale at $529, or Scale at 1,500 runs.
- **Done: `firstrun run --tier NAME`.** The executor and the recovery agent check the tier's cap in the `budget` GUARDRAIL span.
- **Live runs on the typer quickstart, tag `tiercap`:**
  - `--tier scale` ($0.0280 cap): verified 7/7 steps in 127 s with 8 patches, at $0.0201 list price. neatlogs trace `9a29db323b3d054bb2c82e82e080340f`.
  - `--tier free` ($0.0108 cap): stopped at step 4 with `cost budget spent`, after 4 patches and $0.0114. neatlogs trace `06e7f3765141c2f417a862beef5f5134`.
- **Tests:** 255 passed and 2 skipped in the offline suite, including 8 new tests in `tests/test_econ.py`.
  - `--tier free` again, after the cap message moved to 4 decimals: stopped at step 4 with `cost budget spent: $0.0115 of $0.0108`. neatlogs trace `7060f5bd8dbb8cdc6c1dec3830ba7bab`.
- **Known gap: two cost counters.** On 43 runs matched by start time, FirstRun's own count totals $1.5253 and neatlogs totals $1.0989, so FirstRun counts 39% higher. The gap holds after the traces finalized, so ingestion lag does not explain it. The cap checks FirstRun's count, so it stops a run early and never late. Unifying the two counters is next.
- **Done later the same evening:** Ari built the cfo.ai model from `drivers.csv` over the `cfoai` MCP server, with 6 Scenarios. It is public at [cfo.ai/s/_u5lbrHIl9KX_JQE](https://cfo.ai/s/_u5lbrHIl9KX_JQE).

### 2026-10-10, 18:30 to 19:30 IST: The Docs Execution Graph

- **Done:** `run.html` draws a graph from the docs page, through every step, to the fresh-container proof. A failed step branches into its container output, its proposed fix, its rerun and its evidence. Clicking a node opens a side panel with the quoted docs sentence, the command, the output, the change, and every attempt before and after.
- **Honest labels:** nodes read Passed, Failed as written, Blocked, Not run, or Not run: out of scope. Red means the docs are wrong. Amber means the container lacked a prerequisite and the docs were fine.
- **Evidence path:** a toggle shows neatlogs trace, Entire checkpoint, Entire session, Trail and PRs in order. The checkpoint and session pages open without a login. The Trail and the neatlogs trace need one, and the page says so. Entire Graph is not used, because it maps code, not docs steps.
- **Example:** the dbt replay links step 3 to [#10150](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10150) and step 10 to [#10149](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10149) and its bisect comment.
- **Fixes found while building it:** the share tail kept pip download lines and dropped the real error, so stderr now goes last. `report.md` called the step that ended a run its "First Failed Step" even after recovery fixed an earlier failure. It now names both steps, and the root span carries `reported_failed_step` for the neatlogs eval.
- **Checked:** desktop at 1280 px and phone at 375 px with no sideways scroll, the dbt, Dagster and fixture codes, and no console errors. Offline suite: 260 passed, 2 skipped.

### 2026-10-10, 19:00 IST: neatlogs Alerts, an AI Evaluator, and Public Proof Upstream

- **Alerts, created over the neatlogs CLI with write scopes Atharva approved:** "firstrun p95 run cost above Scale cap" (p95 `cost` above $0.035 over 1 day, `56b3b8be`), "firstrun docs breakage or failed verification spike" (compound rule on 2 detections, `74e5d64c`) and "firstrun budget guardrail tripped" (each Budget Limit Exceeded hit, `acd01964`). All three send email. A dry-run test of each returned `simulated` for email.
- **AI evaluator:** "report names the real failed step", an agent judge with neatlogs MCP access, a $0.10 budget and 12 tool calls (`a6aa683e`). An ad-hoc run returned `NOT_FOUND_OR_OPERATION_DISABLED` with gate `tier-c-compute`, so scoring runs only through a scheduled evaluation.
- **cfo.ai:** Ari built the model over the `cfoai` MCP from `drivers.csv`. Under the old $0.50 Scale cap, cash goes negative in month 14. The figures are in [business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md](business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md).
- **Public proof on the 4 upstream PRs:** each got a comment linking the live replay, opened on the fixed step, and the public Entire session. The comments are on [dbt #10149](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10149#issuecomment-6097945132), [dbt #10150](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10150#issuecomment-6097945350), [Entire #2724](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2724#issuecomment-6097945657) and [AccuKnox #671](https://github.com/accuknox/help/pull/671#issuecomment-6097945911).

# Evidence

Every claim in the README has a file here or a public link. Nothing in this folder holds a key.

| Claim | Proof |
|---|---|
| Each run is one neatlogs trace, and v2 beat v1 on the same 4 targets | [neatlogs.md](neatlogs.md), [before_after_traces.json](before_after_traces.json), [neatlogs_runs.json](neatlogs_runs.json) |
| A failed step was recovered and verified in a fresh container | [trace-recovered-entire-v2.md](trace-recovered-entire-v2.md) |
| neatlogs found the agent's own bug, and the fix came over MCP | [neatlogs-investigation.md](neatlogs-investigation.md), commit `3ca6f11` |
| Every commit carries its Entire session, and Trails reviewed every layer | [entire.md](entire.md) |
| The build agents used the Entire graph | [graph.ndjson](graph.ndjson), [entire.json](entire.json) |
| The Entire judge ranks the repo with no excluded work | [jury-selftest.txt](jury-selftest.txt) |
| FirstRun found real docs bugs and opened upstream PRs | [dbt #10149](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10149), [dbt #10150](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10150), [entireio/cli #2724](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2724), [accuknox/help #671](https://github.com/accuknox/help/pull/671) |
| The jafgen release that broke the dbt guide | [comment on dbt #10149](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10149#issuecomment-6096827074) |
| Cost per run comes from neatlogs, one trace per row | [../business/drivers.csv](../business/drivers.csv), [../business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md](../business/BUSINESS_PLAN.md) |
| cfo.ai modeled 18 months from the traces, and the old cap runs out of cash in month 14 | [public cfo.ai model](https://cfo.ai/s/_u5lbrHIl9KX_JQE), [../docs/data/cfo-model.json](../docs/data/cfo-model.json) |
| The plan sets the agent's cost cap, and a live run stopped at it | PR [#15](https://github.com/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/pull/15), neatlogs trace `7060f5bd8dbb8cdc6c1dec3830ba7bab` |
| neatlogs alerts and an AI evaluator watch the runs | [neatlogs.md](neatlogs.md) |
| The session that built and ran FirstRun is public | [Entire session](https://entire.io/gh/HighnessAtharva/firstrun/session/ae05fb29-0c85-4558-9980-42419f08ca9c) |
| Every upstream PR carries a public replay of its run | the proof comments on [#10149](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10149#issuecomment-6097945132), [#10150](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/pull/10150#issuecomment-6097945350), [#2724](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2724#issuecomment-6097945657), [#671](https://github.com/accuknox/help/pull/671#issuecomment-6097945911) |

The patch is one line. 62 63 ## Seven Teams Get a Different Job Out of the Same Engine 64 65 | # | You are | The problem | Run this | You get | 66 |---|---|---|---|---| 67 | **1** | A DevRel or docs lead | Nobody tests the quickstart after launch day | `firstrun ` | A pass or a verified fix, with a PR draft | 68 | **2** | A release manager | A new release of your package broke the docs and you do not know which one | `firstrun bisect --package ` | The last good and first bad release | 69 | **3** | A technical writer | The docs assume tools the reader does not have | `firstrun prereqs ` | A Prerequisites block, proven in a clean container | 70 | **4** | An open-source contributor | You want a first PR that a maintainer merges | `firstrun pr ` | The `gh` commands for the docs PR, source check included | 71 | **5** | An engineer picking a tool | You want to know if the vendor's quickstart works before you commit | `firstrun ` | A time to first success and the first step that breaks | 72 | **6** | A coding agent | You need a loop that checks its own docs work | `firstrun run --resume ` | State after every step and a model-free verify | 73 | **7** | A head of docs | Hundreds of pages, and the code moved under some of them | `firstrun audit owner/repo` | Stale pages with the commits behind them, features with no docs, proposal cards and drafted release notes | 74 75

Jev sorts commits with no conventional prefix when `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is set, and every audit is one neatlogs trace. 87 88 - **Oldest first.** Every page, ranked by the date of its last edit. 89 - **Stale or quiet.** A page is stale when product commits on its topic landed after its last edit, and the report names those commits. An old page that nothing changed under is quiet, so the team can leave it alone. 90 - **Features with no docs.** Each user-facing commit in 120 days is checked against the docs text. A flag or name that no page mentions becomes a "Document this" card. 91 - **Proposal cards.** Document this, refresh this page, feature this, create content around a feature with 3 or more commits, and automate the release notes. 92 - **Drafts.** Release notes for the newest stable tag and up to 3 product highlights, written from commit subjects and pull request numbers. 93 94 `firstrun audit-issue` turns the newest audit into `issue.md`, one checkbox per card, and prints the `gh issue create` command. It opens nothing on its own. 95 96 To audit every week, copy [`examples/github-action/firstrun-audit.yml`](examples/github-action/firstrun-audit.yml) into `.github/workflows/`. The same four targets ran both times. Cost and duration come from the neatlogs traces in [evidence/before_after_traces.json](evidence/before_after_traces.json). Cost is the Sonnet 5.5 list price and is not billed, because the runs use a subscription token. 466 467 | Target | v1 (recovery off) | v2 (neatlogs fix, recovery, verify) | 468 |---|---|---| 469 | neatlogs Python SDK | passed 3/3 | passed 3/3 | 470 | Entire CLI install | failed at step 1, `curl: command not found` | verified 4/4 after 2 fixes, one of them a real docs fix | 471 | Chroma getting started | passed 3/3 | passed 2/2 | 472 | OpenAI v0 README (fixture, Wayback 2023-08-02) | failed at step 6, `openai: command not found` | pinned `openai==0.28.1`, then stopped honestly: the example needs an OpenAI key | 473 474 | Metric | v1 | v2 | 475 |---|---|---| 476 | Quickstarts that end passed or verified | 2 of 4 | 3 of 4 | 477 | Failed steps recovered | 0 | 3 | 478 | Fixes proven in a fresh container | 0 | 1 | 479 | Average tool spans per run | 4.25 | 6.0 | 480 | Average cost per run, from neatlogs | $0.0262 | $0.0200 | 481 | Average run time, verification included | 128 s | 201 s | 482 483 v2 takes longer because a verified fix runs the whole quickstart a second time in a new container. 484 485 The six mistakes the agent made in v1: 486 487 1. The plan changes between runs. The same neatlogs page gave 4 steps, then 3 steps, 5 minutes later. 488 2. The planner invents steps. It added `command -v entire` and `test -f first_trace.py`, which the docs never say. 489 3. The planner writes placeholder steps. Chroma step 2 is `true`. 490 4. A fake secret passes as a step. `export OPENAI_API_KEY='sk-...'` exits 0. 491 5. The planner skips the steps that matter, because they need a key. 492 6. 9 of 16 steps check only the exit code. 493 494 ## What Broke While Building 495 496 - **Git 2.33 hung Entire checkpoints.** The post-commit hook waited 206 s on `git update-ref --stdin`, and the checkpoint was never written. Git 2.55.0 fixed it, and the next hook took 3 s. 497 - **One run split into 3 traces.** The first live run on the neatlogs docs produced 3 traces. The CLI now opens one `firstrun.run` trace around reading, planning, every step and verification. 498 - **Ask-once crashed background runs.** The prompt raised `EOFError` with no terminal. It now returns nothing, and recovery uses the top class. 499 - **Tests exported junk traces.** Each `pytest` run created about 50 empty `neatlogs-app` traces. The test fixture now sets an empty key, and a run after the fix created 0 traces. 500 - **A docs note looked like a docs bug.** On Dagster, FirstRun labeled two gaps as docs bugs. A check of the source showed the page already covers both, in a prerequisite line and a note the planner skipped. FirstRun now opens no PR on Dagster. Every PR draft gets a source check before it ships. 501 - **A cd broke steps three ways.** A leading cd, a cd inside a patched chain, and a file check after cd each failed a step that worked. The container now treats a cd into the folder it is already in as a no-op, and file checks also look from the run root. 502 - **The Entire Brain watcher does not run on Windows.** Brain runs with `--no-daemon` and is refreshed by hand. 503 504 Known limits are listed in [docs/known-limits.md](docs/known-limits.md). Examples: a hung step is not retried, and version pinning covers pip only. 505 506 ## Parallel Agents Built It and Entire Reviewed Every Layer 507 508 - **Build:** a lead session planned the work and ran worker agents in parallel, one track each: fixtures, planner, executor, recovery, verification, report page, then edge cases. All agents ran on Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort. 509 - **Review:** each layer is an Entire Trail, so Entire runners reviewed every commit since kickoff. They found 3 real bugs, all fixed: a secret retry loop, a Windows-only Docker default, and a cd guard that was written but never called. 510 - **CI:** GitHub Actions runs the 246 offline tests on every push and pull request. 511 - **Jury self-test:** the Entire judge plugin, run on this repo with the real start time, ranked it with no excluded work: 3.93 of 5, authenticity 4.5, integrity 5.0. The report is [evidence/jury-selftest.txt](evidence/jury-selftest.txt). 512 513 Planning happened before the event in a private repo. The build log is [hackathon.md](hackathon.md). 514 515

# Demo Video and Submission, Worth 20% Plus the Gate to Everything

The video is 3 minutes or less. The FAQ says it "must explicitly cover neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai: architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning and result for each tool." The script below names all five words for each tool, so a judge can tick every box.

## The 3-Minute Script Has Seven Beats

| Time | Beat | On screen | What you say, in short |

# Packaging, the Report Page and Distribution

This file adds to `12 Marketing Plan.md`. It does not repeat the post times or the tag map. Read that file for both.

## One Repo Folder Holds Every Proof a Judge Opens

The public `firstrun` repo has this shape on Monday. The lead builds it as the work happens, so Monday only fills gaps.

| Path | Holds | Judge it serves |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | One-line pitch, 5-minute quickstart, mermaid diagram, the role of each tool, the numbers table, links | Haimantika, Abhi |
| `hackathon.md` | Build log, rule-change notes, post URLs, the Entire checkpoint link, the honest "planning happened before" line | All |
| `evidence/` | Trace links, one exported failed-and-recovered trace, `graph.ndjson`, jury self-test output | Ajay, Akshay |
| `business/` | `BUSINESS_PLAN.md`, `drivers.csv`, the cfo.ai share link | cfo.ai |
| `report/index.html` | The static report page, built from `runs/` | Akshay, Chetan |
| `tests/` | Unit tests that run with no network | Abhi |
| `runs/` | Gitignored. Raw run output stays local. | None |

**The 10-second README test.** The first screen holds the pitch, one command, one screenshot of the report page and one line per tool. Chetan Raj answers this check on Sunday.

## The Report Page Shows All Three Tools in One Static File

The page is track T6. It is one self-contained HTML file with no server and no build step, so a judge opens it from the repo. It replaces the old "no web UI" line in the spec. A hosted app stays out of scope.

`firstrun report --html` reads `runs/` and writes `report/index.html`. The page has four parts.

| Part | Shows | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Run list | Each target with status `passed`, `verified`, `unverified` or `gave_up`, the first failed step and the time to first success | `runs/*/state.json` |
| neatlogs panel | v1 against v2 as a table: tool calls, cost, duration, failures. A link to each trace. | `neatlogs analytics` output saved as JSON by the lead |
| Entire panel | The checkpoint count, the latest checkpoint link, the `entire graph stats` number | `entire` commands saved as JSON by the lead |
| cfo.ai panel | Cost per run from neatlogs, the price tiers, margin and runway, a link to the share page | `BUSINESS_PLAN.md` summary |

The page uses the light theme and the real logos from `10 Brand and Design.md`. Panel headers carry the neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai logos.

Four rules keep the page honest.

1. Every number carries its source file in a tooltip.
2. A value the page cannot find shows "missing", never a made-up number.
3. The page prints its build time at the top.
4. The page works with the three sample runs in `tests/fixtures/`, so a judge sees it even with no Docker.

**Cut line.** If Layer 2 is not done by Sunday 4:30 PM, T6 ships only the run list and the neatlogs panel. A cut to this page comes before a cut to any tool use (rule F5).

## Writing Passes the Same Gates on Every Channel

Every post, README section and article runs these before it reaches the review desk. The lead runs them. Atharva does not.

1. Pillar check: `python SCRIPTS/pillars/pillars.py --text "<the idea>"`.
2. Slop score: `python SCRIPTS/slop/score.py "<file>"`. CRIT must be 0.
3. LinkedIn shape: `python SCRIPTS/socials/li_format.py "<file>"`. CRIT must be 0.
4. Load-order panel: `python SCRIPTS/loadorder/block.py ...` above the draft.
5. Evidence rule: each post names one real number or one real failure, taken from a file in `evidence/` or a trace. No invented metrics.

20:## Two Detections, One Investigate, One Fix Over MCP
22:1. Detection "docs step broke": a regex on TOOL span output, `command not found|No module named|unrecognized arguments|No matching distribution`.
23:2. Detection "planner invented a step": a regex on the `planner` span output. It flagged the planner spans of the Chroma, Entire and OpenAI v1 runs.
24:3. Investigate (Deep, workflow `firstrun`) traced the invented steps to the planner prompt: [neatlogs-investigation.md](neatlogs-investigation.md).

27:## Three Alerts and One AI Evaluator Watch Every Run
37:The AI evaluator "report names the real failed step" (`a6aa683e`) is an agent judge with neatlogs MCP access, a $0.10 budget and 12 tool calls. It checks that the reported failed step matches the first failed TOOL span, that the failure class fits the container output, and that every patch has a passing verify run. Ad-hoc runs return `NOT_FOUND_OR_OPERATION_DISABLED`, so it scores through a scheduled evaluation.
39:## Evaluations, Sessions and a Second Evaluator Cover Runs and Audits
43:**Sessions.** Every trace about one docs site shares the session `docs:<site>` and names the site as its end user, with the command (run, bisect, prereqs, audit) in the end-user metadata. One session shows a site's runs, bisects and audits together, and an evaluation can filter by site.
45:**A second evaluator.** "audit cards are backed by evidence" (`d1f7c5bb`) is an agent judge with neatlogs MCP access, a $0.10 budget and 12 tool calls. It reads a `firstrun.audit` trace and checks that the root summary matches the span outputs, that each card cites a commit or PR, and that each stale page cites commits on its topic. The audit root span now carries its cards and stale pages in `output.value` for this judge.

Two runs exposed a FirstRun bug: a dev server step (`flask --app hello run`, `litestar run`) never exits, so it timed out. The fix passes a server step once its output says it listens.
